summary: @adminide-stack/utils ships obfuscated payload executed via Function constructor on import
details: The published bundle of @adminide-stack/utils (lib/index.js) appends a hand-written obfuscation stage after the webpack IIFE that is not represented in the sibling source map (which lists only logger.ts/index.ts for a trivial ConsoleLogger). The appended stage uses a custom permutation obfuscator (`spin`/`peel` with NX/SX constants) to reconstruct the string 'constructor' from a scrambled literal, resolves the Function constructor as `peel['constructor']` to avoid naming it, decodes a multi-kilobyte shuffled string into JavaScript, and invokes it with `require` and `module` injected onto `global` (`(global, require)` passed as `(host, ask)`). This runs on every `require`/`import` of the package by any downstream consumer, granting arbitrary code execution with full Node.js module access (filesystem, network, child_process) in the installer's process. The variable names, separators (`^`, `*0`, `*1`, char-code 28), and the Function-via-reconstructed-'constructor' pattern are chosen specifically to evade static URL/API scanning, and the payload lives outside the source-mapped region of what is advertised as a thin logger utility.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
